title: Senior Projectmanager
description:
Jouw Missie bij CCS

Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Samen met je collega’s zorg je ervoor dat wij succesvol onze softwareoplossingen bij klanten implementeren en dat onze klanten een excellente dienstverlening krijgen! Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam.

Voordelen voor de sollicitant

Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar).

Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks.

En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch?


Een voorbeeld van je werkdag

Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen.

Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan.

Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant.

Wie jij bent

De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten:

· Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten;

· Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope;

· Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat;

· Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig;

· Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift;

· Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch;

· Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties;

· Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Naast de genoemde leuke functie binnen een groeiend en innovatief bedrijf bieden wij:

· Salaris: We bieden je een salaris tussen € 5.590 en € 7.958 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur per week), afhankelijk van je ervaring en kennis;

· Middelen: Leaseauto, laptop, telefoon;

· Werkdagen: Je bent minimaal 4 dagen per week beschikbaar, al heeft 5 dagen onze voorkeur;

· Vergoeding voor thuiswerken: Je kunt gedeeltelijk thuiswerken en krijgt een onkostenvergoeding van € 2,40 per thuiswerkdag. Ook krijg je een budget van € 750,- om thuis een ergonomische werkplek in te richten;

· Workation: Je kunt tot 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar vanuit het buitenland werken;

· Leuke teamactiviteiten: Leer je collega’s beter kennen door deel te nemen aan maandelijkse evenementen georganiseerd door ons energieke Fun-team, zoals een pubquiz, Zomer BBQ, wine & beer tastings en movie night;

· Vakantiedagen: Je krijgt 25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om maximaal 20 extra dagen bij te kopen;

· Groei en ontwikkeling: De mogelijkheid om je vaardigheden en verantwoordelijkheden te ontwikkelen binnen de functie, middels opleidingen en Linkedin learning, of door te stromen naar een van de andere functies binnen CCS;

· Vakantiegeld: Jaarlijks 8,33%;

· Voordelen: Je krijgt een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling met een lage eigen bijdrage en kunt gebruikmaken van collectieve verzekeringen met korting. Ook is er een bedrijfsfitnessregeling voor een gezonde levensstijl en een fietsregeling voor duurzaam vervoer.

Waarom CCS?

Omdat wij geloven dat werk meer is dan een baan. Het is een plek waar je jezelf kunt zijn, impact kunt maken en kunt groeien. Het is een omgeving waar je wordt geïnspireerd om het beste uit jezelf te halen en samen te werken aan een duurzame toekomst. Kom bij ons en ontdek wat er mogelijk is als je een carrière bouwt vol passie, plezier en betekenis. Jij bent de ontbrekende schakel in ons team. Word onderdeel van ons verhaal. 🚀

title: Senior Fullstack Developer .NET
description:
Bij OrtaX, onderdeel van Centric, werk je aan software die gemeenten ondersteunt bij het efficiënt, betrouwbaar en transparant uitvoeren van het WOZ-proces. Onze ambitie gaat verder dan het onderhouden van bestaande software. We ontwikkelen OrtaX continu door en investeren daarbij in nieuwe technologie, data, automatisering en een toekomstbestendige architectuur. 

 

Als Senior Fullstack Developer speel je daarin een belangrijke rol. Je beweegt je vanzelfsprekend tussen frontend en backend, bouwt zelf mee aan nieuwe functionaliteit en helpt tegelijkertijd onze applicatie stap voor stap te moderniseren. 

 

Daarbij kijken we nadrukkelijk naar jou om technische richting en structuur te helpen aanbrengen. Niet door keuzes alleen te maken, maar juist door technische vraagstukken scherp te krijgen, verschillende perspectieven bij elkaar te brengen en samen met het team tot goede, gedragen oplossingen te komen. 

 

1. Wat ga je doen? 

Als Senior Fullstack Developer werk je samen met developers, analisten en andere specialisten aan de verdere ontwikkeling van OrtaX. Je bent daarbij niet alleen verantwoordelijk voor je eigen code, maar kijkt ook naar de samenhang en kwaliteit van de oplossing als geheel. 

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: 

 

  • ontwikkelen van nieuwe backendfunctionaliteit in C#/.NET; 

  • ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van frontendfunctionaliteit met één van de grote frontend frameworks

  • ontwerpen en verbeteren van API's, integraties en dataoplossingen; 

  • maken van technische ontwerpen die frontend, backend en data met elkaar verbinden; 

  • schrijven en stimuleren van onderhoudbare, testbare en kwalitatief goede code; 

  • bijdragen aan CI/CD, automated testing en DevOps; 

  • analyseren van complexe technische vraagstukken en deze vertalen naar pragmatische oplossingen; 

  • aanbrengen van technische structuur en bewaken van samenhang tussen verschillende onderdelen van de applicatie; 

  • richting geven aan architectuur- en ontwerpkeuzes en inzichtelijk maken van de consequenties van verschillende opties; 

  • begeleiden van technische discussies en ervoor zorgen dat kennis en ideeën van andere teamleden worden meegenomen; 

  • ondersteunen van collega-developers bij complexe technische vraagstukken; 

  • herkennen en bespreekbaar maken van technische schuld, risico's en mogelijkheden voor verbetering; 

  • stap voor stap moderniseren van bestaande onderdelen van OrtaX. 

 

Je werkt aan een volwassen product waarin continu de afweging wordt gemaakt tussen vandaag waarde leveren en bouwen aan de architectuur van morgen. 

 

Als senior developer help je het team om die afweging bewust te maken. Soms betekent dat investeren in een structurele technische verbetering, soms juist kiezen voor een pragmatische oplossing die past bij de situatie. 

 

2. De technische uitdaging 

OrtaX heeft een bestaand softwarelandschap én een duidelijke moderniseringsopgave. Daardoor werk je niet alleen aan de vraag: “Hoe bouwen we deze feature?” maar juist ook aan vragen als: 

“Hoe past deze oplossing in de rest van onze architectuur?” “Welke keuze helpt ons niet alleen vandaag, maar ook over een paar jaar?” “Hoe voorkomen we dat verschillende onderdelen van de applicatie ieder hun eigen richting opgaan?” En misschien nog belangrijker: “Hoe komen we als team tot een technische keuze waar verschillende inzichten goed in zijn meegenomen?” 

 

Als Senior Fullstack Developer neem je hierin het voortouw. Je kunt een technisch vraagstuk structureren, alternatieven onderzoeken en een richting voorstellen. Tegelijkertijd begrijp je dat de beste technische oplossing zelden door één persoon wordt bedacht. Je zoekt actief de discussie met andere developers, luistert naar argumenten en gebruikt de expertise binnen het team om de uiteindelijke oplossing beter te maken. 

 

Bij OrtaX gebruiken we AI als een belangrijk hulpmiddel bij het ontwikkelproces. Daarbij geloven wij ook dat de developer verantwoordelijk is dat we goede code en een duidelijke architectuur opleveren. Ook op lange termijn willen we beschikken over een goed onderhoudbaar product. Daarbij is AI inmiddels een essentieel hulpmiddel, maar niet zonder input van de developer. 

 

Technisch leiderschap betekent bij ons dus niet bepalen wat anderen moeten bouwen, maar richting geven, structuur aanbrengen en het team helpen betere technische keuzes te maken. 

 

3. Wie zoeken we? 

We zoeken een ervaren developer die zich daadwerkelijk thuis voelt aan beide kanten van de stack. 

 

Voor deze seniorrol zoeken we dus niet naar een backenddeveloper die af en toe frontendwerk doet, of andersom. Je hoeft niet overal dezelfde diepgang te hebben, maar je bent in staat om zelfstandig aan zowel frontend als backend te werken en kunt technische vraagstukken over de volledige keten overzien. Je: 

 

  • hebt een hbo- of wo-werk- en denkniveau op het gebied van Software Engineering, Informatica, Computer Science of een vergelijkbare richting; 

  • hebt ruime professionele ervaring met C# en .NET; 

  • hebt ruime ervaring met moderne frontendontwikkeling en kunt zelfstandig werken met één van de grote frontend frameworks 

  • hebt ervaring met het ontwerpen en bouwen van API's en integraties; 

  • hebt gedegen kennis van databases en begrijpt hoe keuzes in de datalaag doorwerken naar backend en frontend; 

  • kunt technische oplossingen ontwerpen over meerdere lagen van een applicatie; 

  • hebt een goed begrip van softwarearchitectuur en kunt architectuurprincipes toepassen zonder de pragmatiek uit het oog te verliezen; 

  • hebt oog voor aspecten als onderhoudbaarheid, testbaarheid, performance, security en technische schuld; 

  • bent gewend te werken met CI/CD, automated testing en een Agile/Scrum-werkwijze; 

  • kunt complexe technische vraagstukken structureren en terugbrengen tot heldere keuzes; 

  • durft besluiten te nemen wanneer dat nodig is en kunt duidelijk uitleggen waarom een bepaalde richting wordt gekozen; 

  • staat tegelijkertijd open voor andere inzichten en bent bereid je eigen oplossing ter discussie te stellen; 

  • helpt minder ervaren developers groeien door kennis te delen, feedback te geven en samen naar oplossingen te zoeken; 

  • communiceert gemakkelijk met developers, analisten en andere collega's. 

 

Wat maakt jou senior? 

Voor ons zit senioriteit niet alleen in het aantal jaren ervaring of hoeveel technologieën je beheerst.

title: Senior Cloud Engineer
description:
At Luscii, we're creating space for care by developing and improving digital healthcare applications that make a real difference in people's lives through several applications. From Luscii Thuismeten, which helps healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, to OMRON Connect, connecting millions of people with their health data through OMRON devices, and other applications that expand the possibilities of digital healthcare.

Together with healthcare professionals and partners around the world, we're working towards a future where people receive the right care in the right place. As our Senior Cloud Engineer, you'll help shape and modernise the cloud infrastructure behind these applications, building a reliable, scalable and future-proof foundation for millions of users worldwide.

Our applications have different histories, architectures and technical challenges. OMRON Connect, for example, runs on an AWS backend serving several million monthly active users. Parts of its infrastructure still carry legacy, including manual processes, scattered knowledge, inconsistent observability and release processes that make changes slower and riskier than they should be.

We're working towards a more consistent engineering foundation across our applications. Think Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native and event-driven architecture where it adds value, safe continuous deployment and observability by default. We're bringing more senior engineering expertise in-house to turn that ambition into concrete technical decisions, shared standards and a roadmap our teams can own. And that's where you come in 😉

Your role

You will work across our engineering teams, helping shape the cloud infrastructure behind our digital healthcare applications. Your focus will be on making the right architectural decisions, modernising existing platforms and enabling teams to independently build, maintain and improve their systems.

This isn't a greenfield architecture exercise. You will be improving live healthcare platforms while balancing technical improvements with product delivery, security, regulatory requirements and the realities of working with stakeholders across different countries, including the Netherlands and Japan.

  • Own and evolve the Cloud & Backend roadmap, translating the engineering vision into clear priorities, trade-offs and next steps.

  • Work hands-on with engineers on AWS and Terraform, reviewing designs and pull requests and challenging technical choices where needed.

  • Coach and pair with engineers, helping knowledge spread across teams and supporting the growth of seniority and ownership.

  • Work with product owners, QA, engineering leadership and colleagues in Japan to balance technical direction with product, regulatory, security and cost considerations.

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. We stay connected through monthly in-person team days called Assemblii.

  • Flexible setup: Create your own ideal workspace. Whatever works best for you - we’ve got you covered here. We do work from Mondays to Thursdays, as 32 hours per week is fulltime.

title: Product Owner Werkplek & Support
description:
Hoe zorg je ervoor dat ruim 3.300 collega’s iedere dag goed hun werk kunnen doen? Als Product Owner Werkplek & Support geef je richting aan onze werkplekdienstverlening: van Microsoft 365 en randapparatuur tot support en servicedesk. Je bepaalt de roadmap, brengt focus aan en zorgt samen met het team en onze leveranciers dat we sneller, voorspelbaarder en met een betere gebruikerservaring leveren. 

Wie ben jij

Je bent iemand die verder kijkt dan de eerstvolgende sprint. Je kunt zelfstandig een visie en roadmap ontwikkelen, brengt focus aan en durft keuzes te maken wanneer belangen uiteenlopen.

 
Daarbij hoef je niet jarenlang de formele titel Product Owner te hebben gehad. We vinden het belangrijker dat je aantoonbaar eigenaarschap hebt genomen over een IT-product of -dienst en gewend bent om daarin richting en prioriteiten te bepalen. Je krijgt in deze rol veel ruimte. Je stelt zelf de roadmap op, maakt inhoudelijke keuzes en stuurt op verbeteringen binnen Werkplek & Support. Die autonomie betekent niet dat je alles alleen doet. Je stemt keuzes af het team, Servicemanager en teammanager zodat je elkaar kunt challengen op de juiste prioriteiten.

 
Het team bestaat uit collega's die al langere tijd bij Univé werken én collega's die relatief nieuw zijn. Het team heeft behoefte aan iemand die vanuit de Product Owner-rol richting en focus kan geven, zonder formeel leidinggevende te zijn.

 
Onze werkplek is sterk gebaseerd op Microsoft 365, maar omvat meer dan alleen de digitale werkplek. Denk ook aan randapparatuur, lokale ondersteuning en supportdienstverlening. Je hoeft niet zelf de technisch specialist te zijn. Wel begrijp je moderne werkplekdienstverlening voldoende om een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn voor engineers, architecten, securityspecialisten en leveranciers.

 
Een belangrijk onderdeel van je rol is de operationele samenwerking met onze externe servicedesk en andere leveranciers. Samen met het team geef je richting aan prioriteiten en verbeteringen en zorg je dat ontwikkelingen binnen Werkplek & Support goed aansluiten op de ondersteuning van onze medewerkers.


Je voelt je daarnaast thuis in een omgeving die verandert. Je durft bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie te stellen, kunt omgaan met weerstand en neemt stakeholders mee wanneer nog niet alles vaststaat.

Wat ga je doen

Wat breng je mee?
Voor ons is niet je exacte functietitel of het aantal jaren ervaring doorslaggevend. We willen vooral zien dat je dit soort verantwoordelijkheid eerder succesvol hebt gedragen.

•    Je hebt aantoonbare ervaring met het bepalen van visie, roadmap en prioriteiten voor een IT-product of IT- dienst;   

Je kunt verschillende belangen afwegen en duidelijke besluiten nemen en onderbouwen;
•    Je kunt vanuit een Product Owner-rol richting en focus geven aan een team zonder formeel leidinggevende te zijn;
•    Je bent sterk in stakeholder- en relatiemanagement en krijgt engineers, gebruikers, management en leveranciers mee;
•    Je hebt ervaring met externe IT-dienstverleners en weet in operationele samenwerking, samen met het team, verbeteringen te realiseren;
•    Je begrijpt werkplekdienstverlening en IT om inhoudelijk een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn;
•    Je hebt ervaring met het verbeteren van dienstverlening en kunt sturen op snelheid, voorspelbaarheid en klantbeleving;
•    Je kunt omgaan met weerstand, bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie stellen en koers houden wanneer nog niet alles duidelijk is;
•    Je beschikt over hbo/wo-werk- en denkniveau.
Ervaring met Microsoft 365 is welkom, maar diepgaande technische expertise is niet noodzakelijk. Ervaring met grotere transities of het insourcen van IT-dienstverlening is een pré.

Als Product Owner Werkplek & Support ben je verantwoordelijk voor de visie, roadmap en prioritering van onze werkplek- en supportdienstverlening.

Daarbij staat één vraag centraal: hoe zorgen we dat onze collega's prettig, veilig en efficiënt kunnen werken én snel en goed geholpen worden wanneer ondersteuning nodig is?

We willen vooral sneller en voorspelbaarder worden in wat we leveren en tegelijkertijd de gebruikerstevredenheid verder verhogen. Jij vertaalt die ambitie naar concrete keuzes en verbeteringen.

 
•    ontwikkelen en onderhouden van de visie, roadmap en backlog voor Werkplek & Support;
•    prioriteren van ontwikkelingen, incidenten en structurele verbeteringen;
•    vertalen van IT-doelstellingen en behoeften van medewerkers naar concrete prioriteiten;
•    richting geven aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze Microsoft 365-gerichte werkplek, randapparatuur en ondersteunende dienstverlening;
•    sturen op snelheid, voorspelbaarheid, kwaliteit en gebruikerstevredenheid;
•    onderhouden van nauw contact met stakeholders, waaronder Regionale Univé's en decentrale beheerders, en hen meenemen in keuzes en veranderingen;
•    afstemmen met engineers, architecten, security, servicemanagement, leveranciers en andere IT-teams;
•    samen met het team operationeel aansturen van de externe servicedesk en andere relevante leveranciers en verbeteringen realiseren;
•    signalen en terugkerende vragen vanuit Support gebruiken om de werkplek structureel te verbeteren;
•    richting geven aan lifecyclemanagement, upgrades, migraties en vernieuwingen van de werkplek en randapparatuur;
•    kansen rond onder andere automatisering, selfservice en AI vertalen naar concrete verbeteringen;
•    organiseren en voorbereiden van Scrum-activiteiten binnen het team, waaronder sprintplanning, reviews en retrospectives.
 

Je krijgt daarbij ruimte om zelfstandig richting te geven. Dat betekent ook dat we verwachten dat je bestaande keuzes kritisch bevraagt en de teammanager durft te challengen wanneer jij denkt dat het beter kan.

Wat bieden wij

Je krijgt een functie binnen IT Kern Services voor 36–40 uur per week met veel ruimte om zelf richting te geven. Werkplek & Support wordt dagelijks door duizenden collega's gebruikt. De keuzes die jij maakt zijn dus direct merkbaar in de organisatie.

Ontwikkeling vinden we bij Univé belangrijk. Dat geldt voor de dienstverlening waarvoor je verantwoordelijk bent, maar ook voor jezelf.

Het team werkt hybride vanuit Zwolle en Assen. Er is één vaste teamdag per week, afwisselend in Zwolle en Assen. De overige dagen werk je veelal vanuit je standplaats of thuis.

Wie wij zijn

Univé is een coöperatieve organisatie die altijd dichtbij haar leden staat en gericht is op het bieden van financiële zekerheid. Het groeiende bedrijfsonderdeel IT staat voor de uitdaging om het IT-landschap en de IT-organisatie binnen de Univé Formule te transformeren in een wendbare, innovatieve, bestuurbare en toekomstgerichte platform-organisatie.

Schaalbare technologie en processen, optimaal gebruik van datatoepassingen, integratie en standaardisatie zijn hierbij belangrijke doelen. Zo levert IT kostenefficiënt en effectief een strategische bijdrage aan de continuïteit en innovatiekracht van Univé. 


IT Kern levert het IT-fundament waarmee Univé haar doelen kan realiseren. Binnen IT Kern richt Services zich onder andere op werkplekdiensten, eerstelijns gebruikersondersteuning, proces- en servicemanagement en consultancy.
Binnen Werkplek & Support werk je samen met functioneel beheerders, IT-specialisten en een Business Informatie Analist. De servicedesk en het lokale beheer in Zwolle en Assen worden momenteel geleverd door een externe partner.
Je komt terecht in een team met verschillende achtergronden en ervaringsniveaus, binnen een organisatie met veel verschillende belangen en afhankelijkheden. Dat maakt de omgeving soms complex, maar geeft je als Product Owner ook veel ruimte om verbinding te leggen en zichtbaar verschil te maken.

title: Senior Business Consultant
description:
Over Ockto

Ockto is een Nederlandse SaaS-scale-up die organisaties helpt om complexe financiële en administratieve processen slimmer, sneller en volledig digitaal te maken. Met ons platform kunnen consumenten veilig en eenvoudig hun persoonlijke en financiële gegevens delen, rechtstreeks vanuit betrouwbare bronnen.

Maar Ockto gaat verder dan alleen het verzamelen en delen van gegevens. We combineren, structureren, valideren en verrijken data tot complete, betrouwbare en direct bruikbare datasets. Hiermee helpen we organisaties om processen verder te automatiseren, betere beslissingen te nemen en aanvragen zoveel mogelijk volledig automatisch af te handelen (Straight Through Processing).

Onze technologie wordt ingezet door een groot aantal gerenommeerde partijen binnen Nederland, waaronder banken, leasemaatschappijen, hypotheekverstrekkers, online webshops, en overheidsinstellingen. Zo verminderen we handmatige werkzaamheden, versnellen we doorlooptijden en verbeteren we de klantbeleving, met privacy, veiligheid en compliance als belangrijke uitgangspunten.

Met meer dan 100 aangesloten organisaties bouwen we dagelijks verder aan een toekomst waarin betrouwbare data de basis vormt voor slimme, efficiënte en volledig digitale dienstverlening.

De rol

We zijn op zoek naar een Senior Business Consultant die organisaties helpt complexe business vraagstukken te vertalen naar concrete oplossingen en nieuwe zakelijke kansen.

In deze rol combineer je strategisch inzicht met een commerciële blik. title: Data Platform Manager
description:
About the role

As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week.

You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver.

At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive.

What You'll Do

  • Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
  • Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people.
  • Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do.
  • Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source.
  • Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business.
  • Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence.
  • Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge.
  • Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question.
  • Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake.
  • Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's.
  • Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously.
  • Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does.
  • Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams.
  • Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope.
  • Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there.
  • Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases.

  • Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus.
  • Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it.
  • Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

Who You Are

You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head.

You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it.

You enjoy growing engineers, and you understand that leading a small team means doing the work alongside them. Above all, you want to build something durable — a foundation that holds while the company scales on top of it.

title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Finance)
description:
About the role

Every number that reaches our leadership team, our board, and our auditors has to be right the first time — and that is where you come in. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Finance at Destinus, you are the bridge between the owners of our financial data, the CFO, and the wider finance team and the data in our lakehouse. You own how finance data is defined, where it comes from, how it is produced, and how it reaches the people who make decisions with it.

This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what finance needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the finance data in the lakehouse and building the dashboards the CFO and the finance team rely on. You will also improve the processes and systems that create the numbers in the first place, automate the manual work that eats the month, and make our finance data understandable to everyone who needs it, including our AI assistants.

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). We are a fast-growing international group operating across several European entities, and the standards we hold our financial data to are rising just as quickly. Join us in building a finance reporting foundation that is accurate, traceable, and ready for any question asked of it.

What You'll Do

  • Be the go-to contact between the business owners of finance data — the CFO, accounts payable and receivable, and treasury — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on.
  • Build and maintain Power BI dashboards covering cash flow, receipts and collections, payables, and spend across the group, built on certified lakehouse data.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for finance: specify the tables, fields, and business rules — entities, currencies, financial dimensions, intercompany — and validate the result against the ledger before anyone relies on it.
  • Prepare and quality-check entity-level data extractions from our lakehouse and ERP in support of the external audit, and keep audit requests tracked from request to delivery.
  • Define and document finance KPI definitions in our KPI catalog — formulas, inclusions, exclusions, owners, and sources — to a standard that withstands external review.
  • Describe our finance data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: turn recurring spreadsheet work, audit packs, and month-end routines into repeatable processes that largely run themselves.
  • Improve the finance processes and system configuration that create the data, working with the finance team and our ERP specialists, so that issues are fixed at source rather than corrected every month.
  • Help the finance team get more from the tools through training and self-service, so they can answer their own questions.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Controlling, Economics, or a related field.
  • A genuine finance background is essential — experience in external or internal audit, controlling, financial reporting, or FP&A. This is not a data role with finance on the side; you need to understand the accounting behind the figures.
  • Confident with general ledger and subledger structures, trial balances, accounts payable and accounts receivable, bank reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and the principles of IFRS.
  • Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back.
  • Able to explain data to finance colleagues and accounting logic to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance is a strong advantage — the general ledger, accounts payable and accounts receivable modules, and the data structures underneath them. We run on D365, and someone who already knows it will be effective months earlier. An interest in improving how the system is configured and used matters as much as knowing where to click.
  • A track record of simplifying or automating a process, not only reporting on it.
  • Experience supporting an external audit, or working in a multi-entity, multi-currency international group, is a strong advantage.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

Who You Are

You are precise, and you are curious about where a number came from before you are comfortable reporting it — whether that means reading the ledger or querying the lakehouse. You know the difference between a figure that looks right and a figure that can be traced back to its source, and you care about the second one.

You are not content to rebuild the same report every month. When something is manual, repetitive, or fragile, your instinct is to go upstream and fix it rather than absorb it. You enjoy working with finance colleagues who ask hard questions, and you would rather be challenged on a detail than have it slip through.

Above all, you want your work to be relied on, by the CFO, by the board, and by anyone who audits it.

title: Campaign Analyst
description:
Onze missie is helder: beter eten voor meer mensen bereikbaar maken. Als Campaign Analyst in het Customer Retention team speel je hierin een cruciale rol door onze klanten beter vast te houden. Jij zorgt ervoor dat we al onze verhalen, over al onze producten, op de juiste manier aan de juiste klant vertellen. Je bent continu, datagedreven op zoek naar verbetering; zodat we het volgende verhaal nóg beter vertellen.

Wat je gaat doen

Onze retentiestrategie wordt steeds geavanceerder. We sturen niet simpelweg 'een korting' naar alle klanten maar werken met gelaagde acties, inspirerende verhalen en gepersonaliseerde extra’s.

Enerzijds ben jij de analytische drijfkracht achter de executie van onze campagnes. Je bouwt, beheert en verbetert de analytische tooling en dashboards zodat we kunnen blijven leren. Daarmee creëer je begrip van - en grip op - de commerciële impact van campagnes, en alle onderliggende onderdelen (zoals kanaalstrategie, product-samenstelling of klantdoelgroep). Vervolgens vertaal je de verworven inzichten effectief naar succesfactoren, verbeteringstrajecten en/of toekomstige experimenten. Anderzijds werk je inhoudelijk mee. Je bepaalt samen met de Campaign Specialist welk aanbod naar welke klanten gaat, via welk kanaal en met welke verwachting en zet je ook (nieuwe) acties zelf op.

Een aantal van jouw verantwoordelijkheden:

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de performance van campagnes. Je analyseert de impact, en je gebruikt inzichten om toekomstige campagnes te verbeteren, zodat we kunnen blijven innoveren in onze retentiestrategie.

  • Je werkt actief mee met het team: je levert niet alleen de inzichten, maar bent ook zelf verantwoordelijk voor de implementatie van campagnes.

  • Je bepaalt en draait de experimentagenda: welke hypotheses testen we over aanbod, doelgroep en kanaal, en wat leren we ervan?

  • Je hebt ervaring met A/B-tests, holdout-tests en hypothese gedreven werken.

  • Je hebt commercieel gevoel: je denkt net zo graag mee over het aanbod als over de cijfers erachter.

Wat wij bieden

description:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day.   • Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack.

  • Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics.

  • Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow.

  • Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests.

  • Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test.

  • Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work.

  • BSc. or MSc. in systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, mechanical engineering or a related field.

  • 3+ years of hands-on MBSE experience, including building or extending a modelling framework rather than only using existing ones.

  • Hands on experience with hardware system models that encompass multiple subsystems with differing requirements and interfaces.

  • Strong working knowledge of SysML (v1 and/or v2) and at least one MBSE tool, such as Cameo, Capella or equivalent.

  • A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems.

  • Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware.

  • Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries.

  • Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption.

  • Familiarity with SysML v2 APIs, digital thread concepts or co-simulation (e.g. FMI), as well as systems engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 15288.

title: Branch Support Manager - Europe
description:
About Rain for Rent International

Rain for Rent International provides innovative tank systems for liquid management applications. As an internationally operating rental and service company, expertise centers on rental, logistics, and services around the tank, focusing on the core competencies of renting storage tanks, containment systems, pumps, and filtration units.

Your role

We are looking for a hands-on Branch Support Manager ( m/f/d ) to help our teams across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France get the best from our business systems, processes and support functions.

This is not a traditional IT Manager position.

It is a highly business-facing role combining business systems, operational processes, user support, training, continuous improvement and team leadership. You will work closely with our branches and Shared Services teams to understand how people work, where they encounter challenges and how technology and better processes can make their jobs easier and our business more effective.

What you will do

Become a Business Systems Expert

You will develop strong expertise in the applications supporting our European operations and become a trusted point of contact for our business users.

A major focus will be our ERP environment, supporting processes such as:

  • Purchasing and purchase orders

  • Goods and invoice receipt

  • Rental contracts

  • Equipment on-hire and off-hire

  • Recurring and final billing

  • Credit notes and ad-hoc invoicing

  • Customer, supplier and item master data

You will also support the effective use of CRM, Microsoft 365 and other operational applications.

Experience with inspHire, Zoho or Twinfield would be advantageous, but previous knowledge of our specific applications is not essential if you have strong ERP/business systems experience and learn quickly.

Help People Get the Best From Technology

You will work directly with colleagues across our branches to understand challenges, answer questions and identify better ways of working.

That includes:

  • Providing practical systems and process support

  • Training new and existing users

  • Developing SOPs, quick-reference guides and training materials

  • Creating screen recordings and short training videos

  • Building a structured, version-controlled knowledge library

  • Identifying recurring problems and addressing their root causes

Most importantly, you will explain the why, not only the how.

Connect Systems With Business Reality

Good systems only create good information when they are used correctly.

You will therefore work closely with Operations, Sales, Finance, Fleet and other Shared Services functions to improve the quality and consistency of the processes behind our data.

You will help us ensure that operational information, CRM pipelines, rental transactions, margins and management KPIs accurately reflect what is happening in the business.

Listen, Challenge and Improve

Our branches know their business and will bring you ideas and requirements.

Your job is not simply to say yes.

You will listen, understand the underlying need and assess whether the best answer is a change to a system, process, training or something else.

For larger initiatives, you will help structure requirements, assess benefits, costs, effort and risks, and make clear recommendations to leadership.

Lead a Small Team

You will lead a developing Branch Support function, expected to include approximately three team members across business support and IT/helpdesk activities.

This remains a hands-on role. You will lead the team while actively participating in support, training, problem solving and improvement initiatives yourself.

Stay Curious

Technology is changing quickly and we want to take advantage of it.

You do not need to be an AI expert, but you should be curious about tools such as Microsoft Copilot, automation and new ways technology can help colleagues work more effectively.

The Person We Are Looking For

Systems knowledge matters, but how you work with people matters just as much.

You are someone who:

  • Listens before proposing a solution

  • Is patient and enjoys explaining things

  • Can train and support colleagues with different levels of systems experience

  • Builds credibility and strong working relationships

  • Can persuade and influence without relying on hierarchy

  • Is comfortable constructively challenging a request

  • Is pragmatic and realistic about priorities, resources and costs

  • Learns new business processes quickly

  • Enjoys solving problems

  • Is comfortable being visible and close to the operational business

  • Is curious about technology and AI

You should be equally comfortable discussing a process with a branch administrator, working through a systems problem with IT, understanding a commercial requirement from Sales or presenting a recommendation to leadership.

European Scope

The role supports operations across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France.

Regular interaction with the branches is a fundamental part of the position. You should therefore be willing to travel across our European locations, build strong relationships with local teams and spend time understanding how our operations work in practice.

Regular office presence is also expected, currently anticipated at up to three days per week at our office in Potsdam.

Why This Role?

This is an opportunity to shape a developing European support function rather than simply inherit an established helpdesk.

You will have the opportunity to influence:

  • How we use our business systems

  • How we support and train users

  • How processes are standardised across countries

  • How knowledge is documented and shared

  • How new technology and AI are adopted

  • How Branch Support develops as our European organisation evolves

If you enjoy bringing together people, processes and technology and want a role where you can see the practical impact of your work across the business, we would like to hear from you.

Rain for Rent International is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive working environment and welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, disability, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Wie versteht ein Sprachmodell eine Vierjährige? Und wie erklärt es ihr die Welt, ohne sie zu überfordern? Dazu gibt es kaum Paper und keine Benchmarks. Genau da setzt du an.

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. Our agentic engineering playbook is noticeably better because of you — you’ve added or rewritten the skills, rules, and AI review checks the team uses every day, and you lead by example in how you ship with agents.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This is a customer-facing delivery role with a strong technical bias. You'll manage an asset through the full onboarding journey, from initial discovery and technical analysis, through site design and gateway installation, to commissioning, testing and handover into live service.

You won't be expected to design the details of the integration solution or write the software yourself. Your role is to bring together three perspectives throughout onboarding:

Customer: What is the customer trying to achieve, and what do we need from them?

Product: How will the asset operate within KrakenFlex, and what product capabilities and configuration are required?

Engineering: How does the physical asset need to be integrated, connected and commissioned to make that solution work?

  • Work with Product teams to identify where customer or asset requirements do not fit current product capabilities, and ensure gaps, constraints or product dependencies are surfaced early.

  • Feed recurring onboarding challenges, customer requirements and technical integration pain points back into Product and Engineering teams to help improve and scale the GenFlex proposition.

  • Be the primary delivery point of contact for customers during site onboarding, setting clear expectations around what we need from them, what Kraken is delivering and what needs to happen next.

    • Gateway installation and connectivity

  • Proactively manage delivery risks and communicate issues and mitigation plans clearly to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Surface blockers early and drive the right people together to resolve them rather than allowing issues to sit between teams.

  • Maintain clear visibility of the status and health of each site, including technical readiness, product readiness, customer actions, Kraken actions and upcoming milestones.

  • Continuously improve the Generation Flex onboarding process, identifying recurring technical, product or customer blockers and working with Engineering, Product and Operations teams to remove them.

  • A strong interest in understanding how a SaaS product works end-to-end, rather than treating the software platform as a black box.

  • Language: professional fluency in German and English

⭐ Bonus points

title: UX Research Intern
description:
About baesh

baesh is a social platform connecting people in real life through events, communities, and shared interests.

We’re a small team using AI to move quickly from ideas to working experiences. Research is central to how we decide what to build and whether it’s good enough to ship. Your work will help us stay close to people as the technology moves faster.

You’ll work closely with our Head of Product and UX, an experienced researcher with a PhD in emotional and behavioural research. You’ll get practical guidance across the research process—from deciding what to investigate to helping the team act on what we learn.

This is an unpaid mandatory internship for students whose university programme requires a placement.

  • Location: Mostly remote, with opportunities to join research and events in Berlin.

  • Start date: Flexible, depending on your university requirements.

  • Duration: As required by your university, usually 3–6 months.

What you’ll help with

Usability testing and idea validation

  • Help plan and run usability tests on our app and prototypes, including interfaces built with AI.

  • Explore how easily people can discover events, join communities, and create their profiles.

  • Test whether experiences make sense to real people, beyond looking polished or functioning technically.

  • Validate early ideas and assumptions before the team invests further.

  • Identify confusing moments and recommend improvements that make a meaningful difference.

Exploratory research and interviews

  • Help interview existing users and people who haven’t tried baesh yet.

  • Explore how people make friends, find things to do, and connect with communities.

  • Understand their needs, motivations, habits, and barriers.

  • Help write discussion guides and ask open questions that uncover useful insights.

  • Bring people’s experiences into product decisions, keeping the human connection at the heart of how we build.

AI-supported research

  • Use AI to help draft interview guides, usability-testing scripts, and survey questions.

  • Explore how AI can support research synthesis by organising notes, summarising sessions, and suggesting patterns.

  • Check AI-generated summaries and interpretations against what participants actually said and did.

  • Learn where AI saves time, where it misses nuance, and where your judgement matters most.

  • Help us develop practical ways to combine faster research workflows with thoughtful, reliable findings.

Recruitment and ongoing feedback

  • Help recruit participants and coordinate research sessions.

  • Support Friends of BAESH, our community of early adopters who contribute through interviews, user testing, feedback, and feature suggestions.

  • Help create short in-app surveys about specific parts of the experience.

Making sense of what we learn

  • Analyse feedback and identify patterns across sessions.

  • Turn findings into clear insights and practical recommendations.

  • Share research with the product and development team to shape what happens next.

  • Help organise our research so we can build on previous learning.

You won’t be expected to do all of this independently from day one. We’ll guide you, give you feedback, and gradually help you take ownership of research activities.

What you’ll bring

  • You’re enrolled in a degree programme that requires a mandatory internship.

  • An interest in UX research, psychology, human–computer interaction, design, sociology, or a related field.

  • Curiosity about people and a willingness to question assumptions.

  • Good listening skills and an empathetic, respectful approach.

  • Strong communication skills in English.

  • An organised approach and willingness to take initiative.

  • An interest in using AI thoughtfully, including questioning its output.

Preferred, but not required:

  • German-speaking, so you can support research with German-speaking participants.

  • Some familiarity with interviews, usability testing, surveys, or qualitative analysis—university projects count.

  • Experience experimenting with AI tools for research, writing, analysis, or prototyping.

  • An interest in social products, communities, and how digital experiences support real-life connections.

You don’t need previous professional UX research experience. We’re looking for curiosity, care, and a willingness to learn.

What you’ll gain

  • Research mentorship: Learn directly from an experienced UX and behavioural researcher.

  • Practical experience: Contribute to exploratory interviews, usability testing, surveys, and idea validation.

  • Experience with AI-enabled product development: Learn how to assess and improve products when building is fast and informed judgement matters more than ever.

  • Visible impact: See your findings shape the experiences we build and release.

  • Portfolio experience: Develop research case studies, with guidance on what can be shared.

  • Flexible working: Agree a schedule that fits your university’s placement requirements.

  • A small, collaborative team: Work closely with the people designing and building the product.

Interested?

If you have relevant university work or a portfolio, we’d love to see it—but it’s optional.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you'll do

  • Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
  • Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
  • Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
  • Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
  • Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
  • Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

  • You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
  • You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
  • You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
  • You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
  • You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
  • You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.

We'd be thrilled if you had

  • Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.
  • Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.
  • Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You'll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.

Tensordyne Values

  • Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.
  • Own it and get it done. Take responsibility and drive results.
  • Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
  • Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.
  • Value different perspectives. The strongest teams challenge assumptions and bring diverse experience to difficult problems.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Data Serving team that owns the production-grade boundary between Pleo's raw product data and everyone who consumes it, including internal product teams, AI agents, and customers directly accessing their own data. This Senior Backend Engineer role builds and owns that boundary: APIs and the low-latency serving layer underneath it. You will build customer-facing infrastructure where contract stability and latency are non-negotiable, and where the clean abstraction you maintain is what lets every downstream consumer trust the data without ever touching a raw source.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You will report to our VP of Data, and work closely with our Staff Data Platform Engineer, Data Engineers, Product Managers and others Engineers across the business. You'll also coordinate closely with the GenAI Platform and Data Infrastructure teams.

What you’ll be doing

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you will:

  • Build and own the Data API boundary: delivering clean, versioned, and performant endpoints for internal dashboards, customer-facing features, and third-party tools (e.g., Fivetran connectors via incremental syncs and cursor pagination).

  • Design and optimise the read models, indexes, and caching strategies in Postgres (and future OLAP stores) to guarantee low-latency query performance.

  • Build reliable integrations with Pleo’s Kotlin-based product backend services to ensure the serving layer surfaces the correct data required for a customer facing feature.

  • Own the reliability and performance of the services you build: monitoring, incident response, and SLOs appropriate to customer-facing infrastructure.

  • Partner with Data Engineers to define clean contracts between the ingestion/aggregation layer and the serving DB, ensuring read patterns match storage schemas.

  • Partner with the Authorization team to secure APIs using industry-standard authentication and authorization protocols.

  • Build a near-real-time data aggregation service to collect and unify data across Pleo services.

  • Design metadata, lineage, and governance capabilities that make the serving layer explainable, auditable, and trustworthy.

  • Own access control and permission management services, including row and column-level data access with full audit trails.

To put things into context, you can expect to work with the following tech stack: AWS (product side), GCP (data side), Docker, Kubernetes, BigQuery, PostgreSQL dbt, Kafka, Airflow, Python, Kotlin and more!

What you bring

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Strong backend engineering experience building and owning reporting and analytics API services and serving-layer infrastructure.

  • A mindset focusing on reliability, latency, and SLOs.

  • Experience owning API boundary layers including clean endpoint design, versioning, contract stability, and ensuring downstream consumers are never exposed to raw data sources.

  • Strong expertise designing performant read-heavy systems, including relational database optimisation, indexing strategies, materialised views, caching, and API performance tuning.

  • Solid database fundamentals (SQL and non-SQL) and strong SQL querying skills, as well as deep expertise in Kafka.

  • Deep experience with a JVM-based language (Pleo's product backend is Kotlin-based).

  • AWS or GCP with Kubernetes experience. You must be familiar with configuring, deploying and operating containerised applications in a k8s environment.

  • Experience working at the boundary between data systems and product backend services, with a real understanding of the operational differences between the two.

  • The ability to move quickly and independently. This is a hands-on delivery role with clear scope, not an architecture or advisory engagement.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or other regulated product environments.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You are passionate about building systems that serve other engineers.

  • You understand what it means to design, build and maintain services with high performance, availability and reliability requirements.

  • You have a very deep understanding of the data world and know how to bridge the gap between data and engineering.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You need to operate within very large and structured teams with clear hierarchy. This role sits within a small and specialist team with a lot of autonomy.

  • You do not wish to be responsible for services with high availability requirements. You will be held accountable for the quality and availability of those services alongside your team.

  • You prefer to be handed over clearly defined scope of work. You will be expected to define and design the solutions as much as building them.

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you will:

  • Get deep into the current state: the upstream Kotlin services the serving layer will pull from, the internal consumers already waiting on the API (Data & AI Products, GenAI Platform), and any prototype serving logic that needs to be replaced or formalised.

  • Ship the first production version of the Reporting API (a defined set of endpoints with agreed contracts, versioning, and SLOs) with at least one internal consumer live against it.

  • Establish the access control, tenant isolation, and row/column-level security model for the API. You will have proven out low-latency query performance on Postgres, with clear metrics around reliability and SLOs, and established a clear architectural benchmark to understand when (or if) an OLAP layer would ever be necessary.

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis.

  • 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options.

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Core skills test: An async AI-assisted programming test to assess your coding fundamentals.

  3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute chat deep diving into your experience.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

  • We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI - it’s a big focus for us internally too- but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you - not AI - know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.

  • Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • This role focuses heavily on building services for internal / external users consumption. It is absolutely critical to have extensive API design and development experience, expertise in OLAP systems and to be able to work in Kotlin. Ensure your CV reflects clearly of the actual experience you have across those areas.
