  • Coordonner la préparation et la mise en œuvre des plans d’actions correctifs et préventifs.

  • Suivre l’avancement des plans de remédiation et présenter les actions à risque élevé ou en retard aux instances de gouvernance appropriées.

  • Coordonner le programme de contrôle périodique et suivre sa mise en œuvre conformément au plan d’audit défini.

Externalisation, continuité d’activité et résilience opérationnelle

  • Garantir la robustesse et la bonne exécution du dispositif PSEE.

  • Contribuer au pilotage des activités externalisées et des prestataires tiers, conformément aux exigences réglementaires applicables.

  • Piloter les activités de continuité d’activité et de résilience opérationnelle de l’entreprise.

  • Maintenir et tester régulièrement les plans de continuité d’activité.

  • Participer aux exercices et aux réunions de gestion de crise lorsque cela est nécessaire.

  • Identifier les opportunités permettant de renforcer la résilience de Lemonway et sa capacité à maintenir ses activités critiques en cas de perturbation.

Politiques, procédures et formation

  • Évaluer les besoins de création ou de mise à jour des politiques, procédures, formulaires et documents de contrôle.

  • Coordonner la rédaction, la revue et la mise en œuvre des procédures de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques.

  • Concevoir ou contribuer à la création de supports de formation et de sensibilisation.

  • Veiller à ce que la documentation soit claire, opérationnelle, à jour et alignée avec le modèle de fonctionnement de l’entreprise.


Expérience

  • Vous disposez d’au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels, l’ERM, l’audit, la conformité ou un domaine proche.

  • Vous avez évolué dans un environnement réglementé, idéalement dans le secteur du paiement ou en fintech.

  • Vous avez déjà encadré une équipe et travaillé sur la structuration ou la transformation d’un dispositif de gestion des risques et de contrôle interne.

Compétences recherchées

  • Solide connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques opérationnels.

  • Bonne compréhension de l’environnement réglementaire français et européen, notamment des attentes de l’ACPR, des orientations de l’EBA, des exigences LCB-FT et de la DSP2.

  • Expérience du fonctionnement d’instances de gouvernance et de la préparation de reportings destinés à la Direction générale.

  • Maîtrise des environnements de transformation, de croissance ou de scale-up.

  • Expérience de la mise en place ou de l’évolution d’outils GRC.

  • Très bon niveau de français et d’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.

  • La connaissance de l’allemand ou d’une autre langue européenne constitue un atout.

Qualités personnelles

  • Leadership affirmé et bonnes compétences managériales.

  • Esprit structuré, rigoureux et grande capacité d’organisation.

  • Autonomie, tout en appréciant le travail collaboratif.

  • Approche pragmatique, orientée solutions et résultats.

title: Senior AI Specialist (Operations) (x/f/m)
description:
Doctolib is looking for you to join us as a Senior AI Specialist (x/f/m) at our Berlin location, starting as soon as possible.

Doctolib is becoming an AI-native company. We are redesigning the way we work, workflow by workflow, and are looking for people who will not only support this transformation, but actively build it. As a Senior AI Specialist, you will be the technical builder and AI Ops Owner behind AI-powered productivity for our Operations and Customer Success teams.

 

You will work in founder and product mode: you will own a workflow end to end, from context and agent design to evaluation, and continuously take it to a higher level of automation. Our ambition is to move away from manual case-by-case work towards workflows that run largely autonomously while maintaining a high quality bar. In this way, you will contribute directly to our mission of improving healthcare for everyone.

Your Responsibilities

  • Redesign workflows rather than simply automating them: You analyze the most critical Operations and Customer Success workflows, break down time-consuming processes that require limited judgment, and transform them through the use of AI agents. You set clear objectives for autonomy and quality, and continuously develop them further.

  • Build and operate AI agents as products: You develop and manage agents on platforms such as Dust or Claude. Each agent is deployed to production with a defined baseline and relevant metrics such as benefit, usage, and scalability.

  • Knowledge and context management: You deliberately curate the context agents need, from templates to core data. The guiding principle is quality over quantity. You ensure that knowledge sources in Confluence, Drive, or Salesforce are always up to date and well structured.

  • Evaluation and quality assurance: You define quality standards and establish evaluation routines to identify and address weaknesses such as hallucinations or prompt drift at an early stage. You continuously optimize prompts through systematic user feedback and A/B testing.

  • CRM and data integration: You own the interfaces between CRM systems such as Salesforce and our AI platforms. You automate data flows and work closely with IT to unlock new, valuable data sources for our agents.

  • Central interface and enablement: You translate business requirements into technical solutions and bring together stakeholders from Leadership, IT, and Product. You strengthen the team’s AI fluency in the areas of context, agent management, and evaluation.

  • Impact and measurement: Rather than inventing new KPIs, you make the success of AI measurable using existing metrics such as time, quality, and cost, and use these insights to guide the next steps in scaling.

Your Profile

Since production-ready AI workflows and agent technologies are still relatively new, years of market experience are rare. We therefore deliberately prioritize potential over years of experience alone. What matters to us is your ability to learn quickly, your strong product mindset, and your judgment. If you are passionate about this field and bring the necessary skills, we would be delighted to hear from you, even if your profile does not perfectly cover every single aspect.

What Really Matters to Us, Regardless of the Specific Tool:

  • Learning speed and a production mindset: You have taught yourself a new technical field from scratch and built something real that people actually used. You can describe precisely what went wrong, such as hallucinations, prompt drift, outdated data, or costs, and how you solved it.

  • An instinct for evaluation: You do not rely on something merely “looking good”. You define a quality bar and measure against it. For you, automation and quality go hand in hand.

  • Ownership and communication: You take ownership of a problem end to end, prioritize rigorously, feel comfortable with ambiguity, and make technical topics understandable to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Technical and data understanding: You can read and adapt scripts, understand APIs, webhooks, and automation tools such as Make, n8n, and Zapier, and know how CRM data, ideally Salesforce data, flows into AI systems.

  • Strong communication skills: You have a confident command of English and can operate at the highest level in our international environment. German at B1 level is sufficient.

We Are Particularly Interested in:

  • Expertise with agent platforms: You have practical experience with systems such as Dust, Claude, or LangChain. Since tools evolve quickly, we primarily rely on your process understanding and evaluation skills as a sustainable foundation.

  • Technical depth and data fluency: You are proficient in languages such as Python or JavaScript and can confidently navigate Salesforce architectures or BI environments such as Tableau and Metabase to manage data flows effectively.

  • Operations experience: You have solid experience working with scaled Customer Success or Operations teams and understand their specific dynamics.

What We Offer

  • A Germany-wide public transport pass sponsored by Doctolib if you work from the office or in hybrid mode

  • Company-sponsored health insurance with excellent additional benefits

title: Senior Software Developer:in (m/w/d)
description:
KI verändert unseren Job gerade nicht jährlich, sondern monatlich. Und vielleicht merkst du, dass dein Umfeld da nicht mitkommt: KI ist verboten, wird ignoriert oder läuft als „mach mal KI“ nebenher. Bei uns ist das anders. Wir wollen KI nicht irgendwie in den Alltag kippen, sondern wirklich verstehen und als Werkzeug nutzen, das unsere Fähigkeiten erweitert, statt sie zu ersetzen. Wer die Veränderung gestalten will, muss schneller lernen, als sie passiert.

Das heißt auch: Umsetzen ist kein Hexenwerk mehr. Früher war der Job 70, 80 % Entwickeln, das dreht sich gerade. Umsetzung kann man delegieren, Entscheidungen nicht. Darum bist du bei uns der Übersetzer zwischen Fachlichkeit und Technik, und die Ownership für eine Entscheidung trägst du, keine KI.

Das machst du nicht in einem Bodyshop, der dir einen Stuhl beim Kunden besorgt. Und auch nicht in einer Beratung, die nach drei Monaten ein 200-Seiten-Dokument hinterlässt. Wir sitzen über Jahre als tragendes Element in den Entwicklungsteams unserer Kunden, meist in Digitalisierungsteams im Konzern, und schieben dort das ganze Team nach vorne.

Wie du startest

Du kommst in ein bestehendes Projekt mit einem von uns, gehst mit in die Termine und kommst schnell ins Doing, statt ewig Sachen zu lesen. Am Anfang hast du einen Paten, der dich im Team mitnimmt, und einen fachlichen Ansprechpartner. Nach etwa sechs Monaten führst du Termine alleine, setzt Themen eigenständig um und gehst in die Architekturplanung. Stück für Stück übergeben wir dir den Staffelstab, bis du in deinem Bereich die Verantwortung für den Kunden trägst. Leadership heißt bei uns: technische Führung nach außen, nicht nach innen.

Aufgaben

  • Du arbeitest bei einem Kunden, nicht bei dreien gleichzeitig. Mindestens einer von uns ist mit im Projekt, und ihr seid fester Teil der Routinen vom Kundenteam.

  • Du redest direkt mit dem Fachbereich und den Entscheidern. Keine Proxy-POs, kein Projektleiter dazwischen.

  • Du lernst die Fachsprache vom Kunden, modellierst die Domain und setzt sie um, im Backend mit Node/TypeScript, vorne mit React.

  • Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand eine Aufgabe gibt. Du findest die Aufgaben, stimmst sie ab und übernimmst die Ownership dafür.

  • Ein Ticket ist schön. Und dann reden wir nochmal drüber, wie die Fachlichkeit wirklich ist.

  • Wir sagen nicht Ja und Amen zu allem. Wenn was keinen Sinn macht, sagst du das. Diplomatisch, aber klar.

  • Es geht um den Wert, der beim Kunden entsteht. Dafür baust du sauber und sagst dem Kunden transparent, was der nächste Schritt bringt und was er kostet.

Dein Profil

Was du mitbringst

  • Du bist eher in Fachlichkeiten und im Backend zu Hause als beim nächsten abgespacten UX-Feature. Denn sind wir ehrlich, das bekommt man mittlerweile gut automatisiert.

  • Du willst eine Fachdomäne durchdringen und im Großen mitdenken.

  • Du laberst keinen Bullshit, du stehst zu dem, was du sagst.

  • Offenheit und Interesse für die Chancen mit KI.

  • Rund 6 Jahre professionelle Softwareentwicklung, das meiste davon im Backend mit einer typisierten Sprache, am liebsten Node/TypeScript.

  • Node/TypeScript steht bei dir in einem echten Projekt, nicht nur in der Skill-Liste. Und dein letzter Backend-Einsatz in Produktion ist nicht ewig her.

  • Du hast Architektur nicht nur gesehen, sondern auch verantwortet und gestaltet.

  • Du kennst dich in einer Cloud aus, AWS, Azure oder GCP, und kannst sagen, welche Dienste du wofür genutzt hast.

  • Du hast Anforderungen selbst mit dem Fachbereich geklärt, Epics geschnitten und Aufwand mit Risiko benannt.

  • Du hast PoCs gebaut, Technologien ausgewählt und als ADR dokumentiert, Konventionen eingeführt und technische Schulden abgebaut.

  • Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, denn Deutsch ist unsere Domänensprache.

  • Du tickst nicht alle Boxen? Wenn dich das hier anfixt, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Nice to have

  • Du kennst die Baustoffbranche schon von innen. Einer unserer Kunden ist ein Baustoffhersteller.

  • Kubernetes löst bei dir keinen Angstschweiß aus.

  • Domain-Driven Design und hexagonale Architektur begeistern dich.

  • Du denkst eine API vom Vertrag her: OpenAPI, sauberes REST-Design, Backend for Frontend.

  • Du hast KI-Werkzeuge in einem Team eingeführt und weißt, wie man motiviert.

  • Du hast Leute gementort oder ein Projekt schon alleine verantwortet.

  • Du teilst gerne Wissen: Vorträge, Blog, Open Source oder ein Thema außerhalb vom Stack.

Wenn du nicht zu uns passt

  • Du willst ein Team führen. Wir sind zu sechst und planen keine mittlere Führungsebene.

  • Du nutzt KI, um Verantwortung abzugeben, statt deine Entscheidungskraft zu erweitern.

  • Du willst lieber am eigenen Produkt arbeiten als beim Kunden, oder lieber Konzepte malen als selbst bauen.

  • Du willst deine Arbeitsweise durchdrücken, statt aktuelle Praxis zu verstehen.

  • Der Teamtag alle 4 Wochen ist für dich eine lästige Pflicht.

  • Für dich ist es am Ende halt ein Job, und dich treiben vor allem Gehalt und Titel.

  • Du suchst eigentlich das nächste Freelance-Projekt und keine Festanstellung.

Der Prozess

Kurz und ohne fünf Gesprächsrunden.

  1. Erstgespräch mit mir, 30 Minuten remote. Du prüfst uns dabei genauso wie ich dich. Am Ende sage ich dir direkt, wie ich es sehe, und nicht hinterher in einer kalten Mail.

  2. Kennenlerntag mit dem Team, remote, 4 Stunden mit Pausen. Das ist keine Prüfung. Du reviewst Code und erklärst, was dir auffällt. Du baust mit deinem eigenen KI-Setup einen Fix, so wie du wirklich arbeitest. Und du führst ein Kundengespräch im Rollenspiel und lernst das Team in 1:1s kennen. Danach können wir beide klar sagen: passt oder passt nicht.

  3. Referenzen und Angebot. Wir entscheiden gemeinsam als Team und machen dir ein Angebot. Persönlich sehen wir uns spätestens beim Angebotsgespräch oder beim ersten Teamtag.

Nach jedem Schritt hörst du in ein, zwei Tagen von uns. Und wenn es nicht passt, sagen wir dir das persönlich und mit Begründung. Unser Ziel: höchstens zwei Wochen für den ganzen Prozess.

Benefits

Wie wir zusammenarbeiten

  • Wir arbeiten full remote, niemand sitzt im Büro. Alle 4 Wochen treffen wir uns in Darmstadt zum Teamtag. Das klappt gut, wenn du in etwa 4 Stunden bei uns bist.

  • Wir sind keine Family, wir sind gute Kollegen.

  • Warum wir suchen: Wir haben mehr Anfragen, als wir aktuell umsetzen können. Wir wollen nachhaltig wachsen sehen aber in unserer Größe in der aktuellen Zeit eine Stärke.

Unsere Formate

  • Check-in, jeden Morgen: nicht fachlich, sondern sozial. Und es ist voll okay zu sagen: Gerade ist echt nicht cool.

  • AI-Catchup, jede Woche: Wir schauen was letzte Woche in der KI-Welt passiert ist und wie wir unseren Workflow verbessert haben.

  • Weekend Checkout, jeden Freitag: 15 Minuten zum Abschluss der Woche.

  • 1:1 mit deinem Chef, alle 2 Wochen.

  • Retro, alle 2 Wochen, abwechselnd remote und am Teamtag. Daraus setzen wir Experimente mit klaren Zielen und Deadlines um. Dabei gilt Fail Fast: Wenn wir falsch lagen, feiern wir das eher, als uns drüber aufzuregen.

  • Pizzalounge, alle 4 Wochen remote: Pizza bestellen, Wissen austauschen, quatschen.

  • Teamtag in Darmstadt, alle 4 Wochen: am Vorabend ein Social Event, mal Minigolf, Kart fahren oder Axtwerfen. Am Tag selbst Retro und interne Themen.

  • Entwicklungsgespräch, jedes halbe Jahr: Wir setzen Ziele. Wenn du Zeit, Geld oder Ressourcen dafür brauchst, bekommst du sie.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Dein Chef ist Entwickler und quatscht kein Business-Blabla, sondern weiß genau, was du meinst.

  • Ein starkes Team, das TypeScript und React auf Expertenniveau macht.

  • Sicherheit und kein Projekthopping: KI ist wild, aber wir haben all unsere Kunden seit Anfang an und eine gute Basis für die nächsten Jahre.

  • 75.000 bis 95.000 € brutto im Jahr. Wo du einsteigst, hängt davon ab, wie vertraut dir unser Stack schon ist und wie erfahren du in Architektur, KI und Kundenkontakt bist.

  • Jährliche Gehaltsgespräche: Der Inflationsausgleich ist ein No-Brainer, alles on top ist das Ergebnis aus deinen Entwicklungsgesprächen.

Benefits

  • 30 Tage Urlaub und ein unbefristeter Vertrag.

  • 3 statt 6 Monate Probezeit.

  • Teilzeit ab 80 % geht, nach einem Start in Vollzeit.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten, solange du beim Job to be done on track bist und keinen hängen lässt.

  • Ab zwei Stunden Anfahrt zum Teamtag gehen der ICE in der 1. Klasse und die Nacht im Hotel auf uns.

  • Ein top gespectes MacBook. Wenn du der Linux-Gott bist, bekommen wir das auch hin, aber Windows? No way.

  • Essenszuschuss, monatlicher Sachbezug als Gutschein und Firmenrad.

  • Nach Absprache: Mobiltelefon, Unterstützung bei der Kita, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, ÖPNV-Zuschuss, Urban Sports Club und weitere Leistungen über unsere Benefit-Plattform.

Unsere Werte

  • Ownership: Wir übernehmen Verantwortung für die ganzheitliche Lösung, nicht nur für ein Ticket. Wenn du einen Schritt nach vorne gehst, gehen wir alle einen Schritt nach vorne.

  • Verbindung: Beim Kunden sitzen wir als Beifahrer vorne statt auf dem Backseat: Wir gucken auf dieselbe Straße und geben uns ab und an das Lenkrad in die Hand.

  • Wertschätzung: Wir sagen offen, was gut läuft und was nicht, und supporten uns.

  • Entwicklung und Enablement: Was wir lernen, geben wir weiter.

  • Exzellenz statt Pflasterarchitektur: Eine KI kriegt vier, fünf Iterationen gut hin, bei der sechsten crasht es, wenn keiner auf die Qualität schaut. Wir schauen hin und intervenieren frühzeitig auf Hochniveau.

title: Working Student / Intern Finance & Operations (m/f/d)
description:
Your mission

About GENUINE

GENUINE is Europe’s leading TikTok Shop agency, and we’re right in the middle of the social commerce revolution. We don’t just make content. We build shopping experiences that sell, at the speed of a viral trend. We’re growing fast, and so does our Finance & Operations team.

The Mission

Behind every viral LIVE and every creator campaign, a lot of money moves: platform fees, creator commissions, client payouts. You’ll help keep all of it clean, on time and under control. You’ll see how a hypergrowth agency really runs, and you’ll learn more in a few months than in most full-time jobs.

What You’ll Do

  • Follow the money: Match TikTok Shop settlements, fees and affiliate commissions against our records, and catch every gap.
  • Turn data into insights: Build and maintain the reports that show which creators and LIVE sessions actually make money.
  • Keep creators happy: Prepare payout lists, check invoices and make sure everyone gets paid correctly and on time.
  • Keep the books tidy: Collect and organize invoices and receipts so accounting and our tax advisor have everything they need.
  • Automate the boring stuff: Help set up tools that connect TikTok Shop data with our accounting software.
  • Have a say in strategy: Run analyses for pricing, client offers and leadership decisions.

Your profile

Who You Are

  • Student: You’re studying Business, Finance, Economics, Business Informatics or something similar, and you want a working student job or an internship.
  • Excel nerd: Pivot tables and XLOOKUP don’t scare you. You enjoy finding patterns in messy data.
  • Detail lover: A missing cent bothers you, and you won’t rest until you find it.
  • Fast learner: You’re comfortable in organized chaos, you ask questions, and you get things done.
  • Bonus points: You’ve worked in finance or e-commerce before, or you already know TikTok Shop, Shopify, Moss or Spendesk.
  • Language: You speak fluent English. German is nice to have, but you don’t need it.

Why us?

  • Flexible hours: 16 to 40 hours per week, so it fits around your studies or works as a full-time internship
  • Real impact from day one: You’ll work directly with the Finance & Operations Manager and the Managing Director.
  • Inside view: You’ll see social commerce from the inside, at the agency running 60+ TikTok Shops across Europe.
  • Great team: We’re young, international and based in the heart of Cologne.
  • Room to grow: If it clicks, you can stay on longer or move into a full-time role.

· Unterstützung im gesamten Recruiting-Prozess für unsere IFA by Lopesan Zentrale in Schönefeld bei Berlin sowie unsere Hotels in Deutschland und Österreich.

title: Integration Specialist – Electronic Data Interchange (EDI)
description:
We Want You to Grow With Us 

We are strengthening our EDI integration capabilities at Intersnack IT. As our next Integration Specialist – EDI, you will bring your experience in electronic data interchange and your understanding of business processes to support reliable transactions between our business units, trading partners and applications.

Your knowledge of Order to Cash (O2C) and Source to Pay (S2P) will help you translate business requirements into effective integration solutions. Based in Düsseldorf, you will work closely with our Application Service Delivery & Support and Business Transformation teams, business stakeholders and external EDI providers, supporting both daily operations and international ERP initiatives.

What We Can Offer 

This position combines hands-on EDI development with responsibility for integrations that support our supply chain. You will apply your business process knowledge to practical technical solutions and contribute to global ERP initiatives and local EDI rollouts.

If you bring strong EDI expertise and experience with O2C and S2P processes, we can support your onboarding into the Infor M3 integration stack. You will build on your existing knowledge while becoming familiar with our applications, mapping tools and integration environment.

You will join a supportive, international IT team, working alongside colleagues and specialist providers with opportunities to deepen your expertise in integration delivery and EDI operations.

How You Will Spend Your Time as Our Next Integration Specialist – EDI 

You will connect business requirements with the technical delivery and operation of EDI integrations. Your work will span document mapping, integration configuration, rollout support and daily troubleshooting, helping ensure that transactions are processed reliably across our Infor applications and external EDI networks.

What You Will Do 

  • Translate business requirements and trading partner specifications into practical EDI solutions, supporting document flows across Order to Cash, Logistics and Source to Pay.

  • Create and maintain complex document mappings, transforming partner messages into standard XML formats and vice versa.

  • Develop, configure and maintain EDI integrations across Infor M3, Infor ION, Infor OS and Infor Enterprise Collaborator (IEC/MEC).

  • Define and maintain mapping standards, data validation rules and interface specifications, supported by clear functional and technical documentation.

  • Support EDI workstreams within global ERP initiatives and local rollouts across business units, maintaining consistency with global integration templates.

  • Monitor daily EDI transactions, prioritise critical issues and resolve integration or transmission failures to help prevent supply chain disruptions.

  • Analyse performance across EDI networks and clearing centres, identify recurring errors and bottlenecks, and coordinate configuration adjustments and testing with external providers.

  • Maintain standard messages and application interfaces in line with relevant industry standards and data compliance requirements.

  • Collaborate with internal IT teams, business stakeholders and external providers to deliver and support integrations involving both Infor and other applications.

What We Expect of You 

Essential Skills & Experience 

  • Strong familiarity with the document sequences supporting core supply chain processes such as Order to Cash (O2C) , Logistics and Source to Pay (S2P), including orders, invoices and shipping notices.

  • Extensive hands-on experience in Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), B2B integration frameworks and complex data mapping environments.

  • Strong technical proficiency in EDI mapping tools, XML schemas and data transformation languages.

  • Good awareness of global B2B messaging standards, such as EDIFACT, and electronic communication protocols.

  • Proven ability to read and analyse Java code in Eclipse IDE to debug custom mapping extensions and data routing rules.

  • Strong communication and technical documentation skills, with the ability to translate business and trading partner requirements into clear mapping and interface specifications.

  • Ability to work effectively in a complex, collaborative matrix environment with virtual teams in a multi-cultural and geographically diverse setting.

  • Strong analytical mindset, problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, including root-cause analysis of data payload errors and transmission failures, with sound judgement in challenging situations.

  • A strong command of spoken and written English is required, and knowledge of German is considered a plus.

Valuable Experience 

  • Practical knowledge of Infor Enterprise Collaborator (IEC/MEC), Infor ION Framework and Infor OS, including their integration with Infor M3 and the routing of EDI documents into core applications.

  • Familiarity with Mapping Manager and Business Document Mapper within the Infor integration environment.

  • Onboarding customers, suppliers and 3 PLs via EDI.

title: Technical Lead (Core Services)
description:
Technical Lead – Core Services

Build the Future of AI in Financial Services

Aveni is redefining how financial institutions use AI. We build real, production-ready agentic systems that reshape how banks, advisers and financial services firms operate, replacing fragmented processes with intelligent, end-to-end workflows.

We have been recognised as Fintech of the Year for two consecutive years and awarded Best Specialist Technology Service at the Professional Adviser Awards 2025. Backed by leading investors including Puma Private Equity, and commercially supported by Lloyds Banking Group and Nationwide Building Society, we previously completed one of Scotland’s largest Series A rounds. Since then, we’ve continued to grow rapidly as adoption of AI in financial services accelerates, and we’re now scaling our team to meet that demand.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an experienced Technical Lead to take technical ownership of the core services that underpin Aveni’s platform.

This is a senior, hands-on engineering role with responsibility for the architecture, quality and operational reliability of the foundations our product teams build upon. You’ll work across areas including client-data ingestion and preprocessing, CRM integrations and APIs, multi-tenancy, identity and authentication, and data lifecycle and retention.

You’ll lead the technical direction of a team of around six to seven engineers, remaining close to the code while making architectural decisions, setting engineering standards and helping other engineers grow.

Our platform supports regulated financial-services organisations, so reliability, security, auditability and data isolation aren’t afterthoughts — they’re fundamental to how we design and build.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Owning the technical architecture and direction of Aveni’s core platform services.

  • Designing and building scalable, event-driven services on AWS.

  • Developing and evolving our client-data ingestion capabilities, enabling new clients and data sources to be onboarded increasingly through configuration rather than bespoke engineering.

  • Building and maintaining APIs that give Aveni products a consistent way to consume client and CRM data.

  • Designing robust multi-tenant systems with strong data isolation, security and operational controls.

  • Leading our approach to data lifecycle management, including retention, deletion, residency and GDPR requirements.

  • Building resilient integrations with third-party platforms and APIs, including authentication, rate limiting, retries, reconciliation and failure recovery.

  • Making and documenting architectural decisions and representing Core Services in Architecture Review Board discussions.

  • Raising engineering standards across testing, observability, security, reliability and operational ownership.

  • Remaining hands-on with production code, primarily across Node.js and AWS.

  • Mentoring engineers through pairing, code reviews, design discussions and technical coaching.

  • Helping the team make effective use of AI-assisted engineering tools throughout the development lifecycle while maintaining strong engineering judgement and appropriate controls.

What We’re Looking For

Essential

  • Significant software engineering experience, with a strong track record of technical leadership and architectural decision-making.

  • Deep production experience with Node.js, particularly across backend, API and distributed systems.

  • Strong experience designing and operating cloud-native systems on AWS.

  • Experience building event-driven architectures and an understanding of the challenges that come with asynchronous distributed systems.

  • Experience designing production systems with complex multi-tenancy, data isolation or data lifecycle requirements.

  • Strong experience integrating with third-party APIs and designing for rate limits, partial failures, retries and reconciliation.

  • A strong understanding of reliability, observability, security and operational ownership.

  • Experience making architectural trade-offs and communicating technical decisions clearly to engineering teams and stakeholders.

  • A track record of mentoring engineers and raising engineering standards.

  • The ability and desire to remain hands-on while providing technical direction to a team.

Desirable

  • Production experience with Python alongside Node.js.

  • Experience with identity and access management technologies such as Auth0, AWS Cognito or similar.

  • Strong understanding of OAuth 2.0 and authentication/authorisation patterns.

  • Experience building software within financial services or another regulated environment.

  • Experience handling data residency, retention and GDPR erasure requirements at scale.

  • Experience contributing to Architecture Review Boards or similar technical governance forums.

  • Experience establishing or improving AI-assisted software engineering practices.

The Kind of Technical Lead We’re Looking For

We’re not looking for someone who has moved completely away from engineering.

You’ll still design systems, review code, solve difficult technical problems and contribute to production software. At the same time, you’ll create leverage by helping the engineers around you make better decisions and take greater ownership.

You’ll be comfortable asking questions before reaching for a solution, thinking through failure modes as carefully as the happy path, and balancing architectural quality with the realities of delivering software in a fast-growing business.

You don’t need to have used every AWS service or technology in our stack. What matters more is that you understand the underlying engineering problems, can explain the trade-offs behind your decisions, and have successfully operated the systems you’ve helped design.

  • Company-wide off-sites

  • Private health and dental care

  • Potential share options

At Aveni, we believe that diversity drives innovation. We’ve built our business to ensure an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best work. If you’re passionate about technology and its ability to drive positive change for the future of financial services, we’d love to hear from you. About the Role

As Content Lead at Dex, you'll write and publish everything that carries our name.

You'll own Dex's channels: the website, social, email, our events programme and blog. You'll take a content strategy that already exists and turn it into a steady, high-quality output.

This is a job for someone who writes fast and well, and who thinks past the draft. The copy is half of it. The other half is knowing where a piece needs to land, what it needs to look like to get found, and what it should do to the reader once it does.

You'll work closely with Marketing, Growth, Design and Product.

You'll have real autonomy and very little bureaucracy.

What You'll Do

  • Own the channels. The publishing calendar across site, social, email and the blog is yours. You decide what runs, when, and in what order.

  • Write across every format. LinkedIn and X posts, campaign and event emails, landing pages, product and lifecycle copy, event pages and follow-ups, articles and explainers. A 90-word page and a 1,500-word argument in the same afternoon, both sounding like us.

  • Think in distribution, not just drafts. Every piece gets planned around where it will be read: why a piece lands on Hacker News and dies on LinkedIn, which newsletters and communities our audience already trusts.

  • Write for search and AI answers. We have a GEO and SEO spec built with our search partner: answer-first structure, extractable formatting, clean internal linking, author entity pages. You'll write to it and help us improve it.

  • Carry the events programme. Copy and collateral for our event series, before, during and after, and the follow-up sequences that turn attendance into something.

  • Work the numbers. Track performance and report back on the metrics that matter across our owned blog and organic social media channels.

  • Use AI properly. Research, outlining, structuring, first passes, repurposing, quality checks. We'll give you all the Claude tokens you can use. We will not ship anything that sounds like AI wrote it, and we'll ask you how you draw that line.

  • Guard the voice. You'll be the most frequent user of our tone of voice and audience research, and the person most responsible for whether it holds up in public.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years writing in-house or at an agency, ideally for a technical or developer audience, ideally in a start-up where you had to build the process as well as the output

  • Genuine range across formats and lengths, evidenced by a portfolio of published work

  • A real view on distribution: where our audience discovers, consumes and shares things, and what a piece needs to look like to survive that journey

  • Working knowledge of SEO and how AI search surfaces content, enough to write to a spec and challenge it

  • Fluent with AI tools across research, outlining and iteration, with judgement about where the machine stops and you start

  • Commercial literacy. You can connect a piece of content to an outcome and look beyond vanity metrics

  • Editorial judgement under your own steam. You can take a rough steer and come back with something better than the brief

  • A proactive communicator who works well without supervision and asks for what they need

Nice to Have

  • Any technical background, formal or self-taught

  • Experience marketing to engineers, developers or another audience that punishes fluff

  • Experience with content for events and communities

  • Basic design or motion skills, enough to get a social asset out without waiting

Not a strategy job. The strategy exists and you're here to execute it, though you'll influence it constantly and we expect you to argue with it.

Not a pure writing job. Publishing, sequencing, formatting, distribution and measurement are all yours.

description:

The company is renowned for providing a positive and entrepreneurial work environment. We are honored to have received the "Happy at Work" and "Tech at Work" labels every year since 2019. 

The Role:

Lini is DiliTrust's proprietary AI engine, powering Ask Lini, Risk Detector, Document Summarization, Minute Generation, and every AI capability across the suite.

We are building a dedicated squad around it and are looking for a strong Software / Product Engineer, with a focus our platform architecture, to help us bring it to the next level. 

As a Software Engineer work at the intersection of AI, product, and engineering. You will contribute to building, improving, and scaling the features that make Lini a reliable and powerful AI layer across the entire DiliTrust suite. 

We are looking for an engineer who writes clean, production-ready code and is comfortable taking ownership of features end-to-end, from technical design to deployment. We also care about how you think about AI: whether you bring genuine curiosity to the product, and whether you can translate a model capability into a great user experience. 

Missions

  • Write specifications as the durable asset of the project. Executable acceptance criteria, and — crucially — the non-functional requirements that specs almost never carry: data classification, endpoint × role authorization matrix, volumetry assumptions, latency and throughput budgets. These are the requirements whose later correction is superlinear, so they get decided before generation, not after.
  • Freeze the contracts before any fan-out. API schemas, types, module boundaries, invariants. Agents do not negotiate an interface in the hallway: each will make a plausible and incompatible assumption, discovered at integration.
  • Pilot coding agents with a tight brief and a bounded context — narrow tasks, defined input and output artifacts, explicit stop conditions and budgets, full traceability of what produced each change.
  • Keep producer and verifier separate. You do not sign off alone on generation you piloted, and you act as independent verifier on your peers' slices — with an adversarial brief ("find what breaks against this spec"), never "confirm this looks fine".
  • Build the asymmetric gates that make the slice safe at volume — expensive to satisfy, cheap to check: property tests, contract tests, query-count and allocation budgets, execution-plan checks, policy-as-code, backward-compatibility proofs. Written before the implementation exists, so the agent closes the feedback loop itself without consuming human attention.
  • Use code reading as a calibration instrument, not as a gate. Sample deliberately, by risk zone, to measure the real defect rate of the generator-plus-gates pair and to keep the team's mental model of its own system alive.
  • Keep work-in-progress low. Capped PR size, thin vertical slices, trunk-based with very short branches, feature flags over long-lived branches, CI as the agent's first task rather than its last. More features in flight does not mean faster delivery when the bottleneck is verification.
  • Design for blast radius. Reversibility, progressive delivery, structured logs, traces, metrics and instrumentation generated as a matter of course. On many paths, detecting in five minutes beats three days of review that prevents nothing.

Requirements

Being based in France with full working rights. Fluent in French and English.

Experience & Seniority:

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a significant portion spent building and operating B2B SaaS platforms in production
  • Proven ownership of features across their full lifecycle — design, delivery, iteration, maintenance — on long-lived, multi-year products
  • Strong background in complex, scalable web architectures, including real modularity: you have seen where coupling stops parallel work dead

AI-Native Practice:

  • Demonstrated, sustained use of coding agents in production work — not autocomplete, but delegated implementation with review and accountability
  • A concrete, articulated view of where generated code fails: correlated defects rather than idiosyncratic ones, uniform surface quality that destroys the usual "look here" review signals, plausibility with no author to interrogate
  • Comfort being accountable for code you did not author, and the discipline to refuse a change you cannot explain

Verification & Quality:

  • Real fluency in property-based testing, contract testing, and deriving tests from the specification rather than from the code
  • Test-data strategy, including maintaining a volumetrically representative dataset as part of the verification apparatus — not a nice-to-have
  • Instinct for the difference between a rigorous check and a scalable one: does the cost of checking grow with the volume produced?

Security & Performance (non-negotiable on this role):

  • Authorization modelling in multi-tenant systems, and why declarative, centrally enforced authorization beats reviewing each endpoint. Generated code reliably checks who you are and regularly forgets whether you are allowed
  • Awareness of the attack surface specific to an agent-assisted pipeline: prompt injection through ticket descriptions, code comments and dependency READMEs; supply-chain risk on hallucinated package names; least privilege for non-human identities; and the most frequent risk of all — production data or proprietary code leaking into the development loop
  • Performance as a measured number rather than a code-reading opinion: query budgets per HTTP request, N+1, unbounded result sets, missing indexes on new query paths, network calls in loops, execution-plan review. These are invisible at test-data scale and expensive in production

Product & Team Collaboration:

  • Excellent written communication — specification writing is now a core engineering skill on this role, not documentation overhead
  • Extensive experience working directly with product managers, designers and stakeholders in a product-oriented setup
  • Strong sense of ownership and sound judgment on risk: what to build, what not to build, what residual risk is acceptable and why

Education:

  • Master's degree in Engineering or equivalent practical experience in senior SaaS environments

What this role is not

We would rather say it up front:

  • It is not a prompt-engineering role, and it is not an ML/LLM research role.
  • It is not a role where green tests are sufficient evidence. On security and performance, "the spec is met and the tests pass" is not a weak signal — it is a null one.
  • It is not a ticket queue. The profile that shrinks in an AI-native team is the one whose value was implementing assigned tickets between two boundaries.

Our Tech Stack

  • Backend: Node.js / TypeScript
  • Frontend: Vue.js 3
  • Database: PostgreSQL, MariaDB
  • DevOps: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
  • Cloud: GCP

Engineering apparatus you will use and help build: coding agents orchestrated deterministically in CI, aspect-scoped verification agents (authorization, performance, spec conformance, dependencies), policy-as-code, property-based and contract testing, volumetric test datasets, load and endurance gates on critical paths, feature flags, progressive delivery and end-to-end tracing.

What we offer

  • Join a fast-growing company in a friendly, international environment — engineering primarily in Paris, with further engineering presence in Berlin, Montreal and Wilmington (DE), and offices across France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Canada, the USA, Mexico and Dubai;
  • Our "Remote Policy" guarantees that you can find the right balance between "Onsite" and "Remote";
  • Last but not least, all the day-to-day benefits of the CSE, luncheon vouchers, profit sharing bonuses, etc...

Recruitment process

  • Interview with the Engineering Manager (1h)
  • Technical interview (1h30) — two parts: turning an ambiguous requirement into a specification with executable acceptance criteria, then an adversarial review of an agent-generated diff against that specification
  • Interview with the CTO (45 mins)

Scope

Field marketing takes our global strategy into each market through four areas: pipeline support, partner marketing, events, and content. You'll build and lead a team of 3 Field Marketing Managers (North America, France & MEA, Italy, Spain & DACH).

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About the role

Linkup is the web search engine built for AI. Our infrastructure crawls, indexes and serves the live web to AI agents, and it’s scaling fast.

We’re looking for a top‑tier Machine Learning Engineer to join Linkup and work hand‑in‑hand with our CTO, Denis Charrier, and the rest of the tech team.

Your core responsibilities will be to:
Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

  • Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

  • Bring new ranking signals into the engine, beyond pure relevance

  • Build the evaluation framework that tells us what really improves search quality

  • Optimize model serving for latency and GPU cost

  • Turn customer and benchmark feedback into ranking improvements, with clear before/after numbers

     
 

Requirements

You’re a great match if you:

  • Are excited to help build Google for AI agents- and believe in Linkup’s mission

  • Have strong hands-on experience in information retrieval, ranking or search in production.

  • Build rigorous evals and check the data behind every number

  • Care about latency, cost and reliability as much as model quality

  • Thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment

 

Example Projects

  • Ship a new ranking model to production and prove the gain on our eval sets

  • Push our models to the next level: better answers, lower latency, lower cost per query

  • Build and maintain the evaluations framework that measures every change to our search engine

 

Our Stack

Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, Ray, Spark / Databricks, Vespa, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Terraform

Details

The ideal candidate will play a central role in our engineering team, partnering closely with the founders. The models you ship will decide what thousands of AI products read every day.

We offer a flexible remote‑work policy- see the details here.

Join us and leverage your expertise to push the boundaries of AI!

 

About Linkup

 

Our Vision

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

 

Our Mission

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

 

Our Culture

Our culture is built on the following values:

  • Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

  • Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

  • Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

  • Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

  • Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

 

Our Team

We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

  • Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen, an open source search engine.

  • Denis Charrier- Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

  • Boris Toledano- Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

title: PR Manager DE
description:
A fight lasts minutes. A great story travels much further.

The comeback nobody saw coming. The rivalry that divides an arena. The person behind the fighter, with a story that deserves to reach people who have never watched MMA.

At OKTAGON, those stories are everywhere.

We’re building a sports brand with international ambitions, passionate fans and events that bring thousands of people together. Germany is a major part of that journey. And we’re looking for a PR Manager who knows how to make our stories matter to German media.

Someone who can earn the trust of a sports editor, spot an angle for a business title and understand why a digital format might reach an audience a traditional press release never will.

You’ll help decide which stories we tell, who we tell them to and how far they go.

Your stories need to travel beyond the cage.

Sports media will be your home ground. But your curiosity should take you further.

A fighter’s journey can belong in a mainstream interview. Our growth can start a business conversation. Training, personality and culture can open doors to fitness and lifestyle coverage.

You’ll find those opportunities and turn them into pitches that give each outlet a reason to care.

Here’s what you’ll take ownership of:

  • Build real relationships with German media. Develop and maintain a network across sports, digital and mainstream outlets. Get to know the journalists, their audiences and the stories they actually want.

  • Earn coverage for OKTAGON, our events and our fighters. Create opportunities around upcoming fights and recognise stories that deserve attention outside the event calendar.

  • Find new routes to our audience. Follow how the media landscape is changing, from digital publishers and podcasts to emerging editorial formats. Know where a story will work and adapt it accordingly.

  • Create sharp German press materials. Write press releases, translate and localise event Media Info Cards, research fight cards and prepare tailored angles for individual outlets.

  • Make interviews happen. Connect journalists with fighters, coordinate opportunities and prepare written interviews when needed.

  • Get the right assets into the right hands. Distribute photos, video and relevant information, including captioned fight photography for dpa-picture alliance and Imago.

  • Keep the foundations organised. Own accreditations, maintain the media database and keep fighter information accurate and up to date.

  • Show what your work achieves. Monitor online and offline coverage, prepare monthly reports and summarise results after German events. Use what you learn to improve the next campaign.

  • Keep our communication connected. Work closely with the PR lead, Marketing DE and Social Media so our messaging stays consistent, including across German-language video content.

When fight week starts, you’re in the middle of it.

The plans are ready. The journalists arrive. Interview requests change. A result creates a new headline.

You’ll be the person who keeps media operations moving.

At German events, that means overseeing accreditations and the media room, coordinating interviews, supporting weigh-ins and press conferences, and making sure journalists have what they need before and after the fights. Where needed, you may also moderate a press conference.

You’ll handle post-fight releases, follow-ups and coverage reviews. During selected events outside Germany, you’ll be available for relevant German media requests and breaking stories.

And when a sensitive situation comes up, you’ll be the first point of contact for German media, working closely with the PR lead on the response.

This role includes travel and weekend work. Fight weeks can run from Thursday through Sunday, and you need to be comfortable with the pace and responsibility that come with live events.

What you bring into the team

You already know how a newsroom works. You understand deadlines, editorial judgement and the difference between a story we want to tell and a story someone will want to publish.

We’re looking for:

  • At least 2–4 years of relevant experience in PR or sports journalism. You’ve pitched stories, worked with journalists and delivered under pressure.

  • An existing network in German sports newsrooms. Relationships you can build on, alongside the initiative to open new doors.

  • Native-level German and very good English. Your German writing is precise, natural and adaptable. You’re comfortable collaborating with an international team in English.

  • Strong editorial instincts. You can spot an angle, ask the useful question and turn a complicated story into a clear pitch.

  • Digital confidence. You understand how people discover and consume stories today and stay curious about what is changing.

  • Independence and ownership. You can organise your work remotely, follow through on commitments and keep colleagues informed.

  • Willingness to travel and work weekends. You want to be there when the action happens.

An interest in MMA or combat sports, experience with press conferences and crisis communication, and a driving licence are all advantages.

You don’t need to know every fighter’s record on day one. You do need the curiosity to learn the sport and understand the people in it.

Ready to tell the next story?

Send us your CV (English version) or LinkedIn profile and a few examples of your work: coverage you secured, a campaign you helped deliver or journalism you’re proud of.

Tell us what you contributed and why it worked.

We’d also love to hear what interests you about bringing OKTAGON’s stories to German audiences.

Let’s talk.

title: Senior Manager, Customer Support, Deliveroo Operations
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Our mission is to transform the way people shop and eat, connecting consumers, restaurants, shops, and riders to bring the neighbourhood to their door. We're redefining convenience by giving customers the ability to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.

Deliveroo is a technology-driven company at the forefront of one of the world's most dynamic industries. We are a relatively small team making a very large impact, moving fast, valuing ownership, and tackling some of the most interesting challenges in global commerce. We're driven by innovation, autonomy, and the ambition to deliver exceptional experiences for our customers, partners, and riders alike.

What You'll Be Doing

You will own frontline operational performance across two closely linked parts of Deliveroo's customer support network: an in-house Global Escalations team of around 50 agents based across the UK and Georgia, and the outsourced network delivering support on our behalf through three BPO partners and three Shared Service Centres, circa 1,500 agents across multiple locations, including the team leads and ops managers embedded within those outsourced functions.

Global Escalations sits at the heart of Deliveroo's most critical customer moments. The team manages our most sensitive, high-risk, and high-impact contacts, including complaints escalated to the Executive team. As the leader directly accountable for this recovery-focused centre of excellence, you will ensure the team operates with exceptional skill, judgement, and empathy, protecting Deliveroo's reputation, driving improvement through root cause analysis, and embedding a culture of integrity and customer-first recovery across the organisation.

For the outsourced network, you own how performance is delivered day to day, working closely with the team leads and ops managers embedded in each BPO and Shared Service Centre, not just the vendor relationship at arm's length. You own the operational rigour needed to make the network the best in class, from an experience and consistency perspective, across every market it supports.

Your key objective is to drive qualitative improvements to the customer experience, measured through CSAT, while balancing cost metrics like average handling time (AHT) and refund costs, rather than trading one off against the other. You will be the voice of Support to Deliveroo's market General Managers, taking full accountability for the Support experience in your markets, and you will partner closely with cross-functional Support & Operations teams, including Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy, to drive initiatives that positively impact all three sides of the marketplace: customers, riders, and merchants.

You Will…

  • Own frontline operational performance delivered through the in-house Global Escalations team (UK and Georgia) and the outsourced network (3 BPOs, 3 Shared Service Centres, circa 1,500 agents), including the team leads and ops managers within those outsourced functions
  • Lead and develop the Global Escalations team directly, managing our most sensitive and reputation-critical contacts with judgement, empathy, and rigorous root cause analysis
  • Drive qualitative improvements to the customer experience, tracked through CSAT, while balancing cost metrics like AHT and refund costs
  • Act as the voice of Support to Deliveroo market GMs, taking full accountability for the Support experience in your markets and representing their priorities back into the function
  • Partner with Support & Operations cross-functional teams, including Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy, to drive initiatives that improve the experience for customers, riders, and merchants
  • Design and run performance frameworks that hold BPO and SSC team leads and ops managers accountable for quality, SLA adherence, and CSAT, fostering a culture of partnership rather than pure oversight
  • Standardise processes and playbooks across outsourced partners and sites where it drives consistency, while respecting genuine market and site-specific differences
  • Diagnose and help bring down attrition and quality issues across the outsourced network, working with BPO and SSC leadership on the retention, engagement, and workforce planning changes needed
  • Partner with Product and Technology to shape the roadmap for customer support systems and channel strategy, identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency and automation across both in-house and outsourced teams
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across HR, Legal, and Policy to ensure service delivery evolves in line with business priorities
  • Drive data-informed improvement through analysis of contact drivers, escalation themes, and customer sentiment, translating insight into action for both Global Escalations and the outsourced network
  • Represent the function at relevant Weekly Business Reviews and senior forums, providing visibility on performance, risk, and recovery across both the in-house team and the outsourced network
  • Participate in the 24/7 Leadership Team on-call rota
  • Shape functional strategy and set OKRs for contact centre Support across Deliveroo markets, growing the remit from directing your own team to leading leaders, in line with DoorDash's Team Management career framework
  • Grow and develop the managers and leaders within your network, including Team Leads inside Global Escalations and the team leads and ops managers at each BPO and Shared Service Centre, building the next generation of people leaders

Our humble expectations

  • Extensive contact centre, BPO, or shared service centre leadership experience in a fast-paced, consumer-facing environment
  • Proven experience managing outsourced or vendor relationships at scale, including the team lead and ops manager layer embedded within partner organisations, not just the commercial relationship
  • Experience leading escalations or complaint handling in a reputation-sensitive environment, with strong judgement and the ability to drive recovery from the most sensitive customer moments
  • A track record of bringing consistency and governance across multiple outsourced partners while respecting genuine local and market differences
  • Experience diagnosing and reducing attrition while improving quality, in a large-scale, multi-site support operation
  • A data-driven approach to balancing customer experience (CSAT) against cost metrics such as AHT and refund rate, without trading one off blindly against the other
  • Experience representing a support or operations function to senior commercial stakeholders, such as General Managers or market leadership, taking full accountability for their experience of the function
  • Experience partnering with cross-functional teams such as Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy to drive improvements across a multi-sided marketplace
  • Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and work cross-functionally with Product, Legal, Policy, and People teams
  • Strong analytical ability, comfortable turning contact driver, escalation, and sentiment data into action
  • Strong people leadership skills, with experience building and developing a dispersed in-house team and driving performance indirectly through partner leadership
  • A self-starter mindset, a can-do attitude, and willingness to be hands-on in a fast-moving, multi-geography environment
  • Proven strategic mindset with a track record of shaping and executing operational strategies across multiple markets and vendors
  • Deep operational understanding, including customer service design, vendor management, and process optimisation
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver results in high-volume, complex environments with multiple priorities
  • Experience partnering with Product and Tech to drive tooling, system, and automation improvements
  • A mindset focused on continuous improvement, customer advocacy, and operational excellence
  • Demonstrated ability to operate at a 'leads leaders' level per DoorDash's Levels and Expectations framework (Team Management track): shaping strategy and OKRs beyond your own team, and developing managers who in turn develop their own teams
  • Meets the senior people-leadership bar DoorDash expects at this level: effectively leads a high-performing team, fosters a culture of belonging and engagement, and takes full accountability for the people outcomes of a large, dispersed organisation

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

As our Community Lead reporting to the Head of Marketing, you’ll shape how healthcare professionals connect, learn from one another and drive change across the NHS. You’ll turn organic momentum into a scalable community that measurably drives product adoption, peer-to-peer learning and brand trust.

description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.

You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitised, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.

Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.

And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.

You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

💻 What will you do

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.

  • Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

  • Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.

  • Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.

  • Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.

  • Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.

  • Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.

  • Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

🥷 Your skills

Non-negotiables

  • You ship end to end: a track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.

  • Genuine customer obsession: a real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.

  • Product taste and craft: the bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.

  • A point of view on agentic product design: how an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.

  • You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.

  • Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.

  • Trade-off fluency: you weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.

  • Strong analytical instinct: you define the metric, build the view, read it, and act, without waiting for a data team.

  • You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.

Strong signals we look for

  • Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.

  • Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.

  • Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

  • You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.

  • Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.

  • Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.

Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional.

🪅Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + equity. We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win.

  • Annual global offsite in New Zealand. Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1-2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch.

  • Parental leave: Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work (four days on full pay for your first three months back).

  • Team lunches: Lunch provided daily (Monday to Friday) in the office

  • Flexible working hours: We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office.

  • Season openers & events: We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours.

  • Healthy body, healthy mind: Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use on gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions; anything that you or your family, need.
